candidate_relations.reason: Cardiac tamponade is not described and is a different hemodynamic diagnosis from secondary cardiac lymphoma.
Lymphomatous cardiac involvement names the same secondary cardiac lymphoma object given prior DLBCL and atrial masses.
Chemotherapy-related cardiotoxicity is a different myocardial injury mechanism from lymphomatous masses.
Chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy does not account for FDG-avid right atrial masses.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: chemo cardiomyopathy vs secondary cardiac lymphoma

candidate_relations.reason: Restrictive cardiomyopathy describes a possible filling pattern, not secondary cardiac lymphoma.
Cardiac lymphoma is the correct family but omits the required secondary/extracardiac-origin specifier.
Pulmonary embolism is a different cause of dyspnea from right atrial lymphomatous masses.
Malignant cardiac neoplasm is a parent category and omits secondary lymphoma identity.
Cardiac amyloidosis is a different infiltrative cardiomyopathy from lymphoma.
Cardiac metastasis captures secondary cardiac tumor spread but omits lymphoma/DLBCL identity.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the underlying histology but omits secondary cardiac involvement.
Secondary cardiac lymphoma matches the full reference object.
Atrial fibrillation is not the described ECG pattern of prolonged P waves and shortened PR segment.
Cardiomyopathy is a nonspecific functional label for the NT-proBNP elevation, not secondary cardiac lymphoma.
Restrictive cardiomyopathy secondary to lymphoma is a physiologic consequence rather than the mass-infiltrative diagnosis.
Cardiac sarcoidosis is a different inflammatory infiltrative disease.
Recurrent cardiac infiltration of DLBCL is the same secondary cardiac lymphoma object.
Lymphomatous pericarditis captures adjacent pericardial FDG uptake but omits the dominant right atrial myocardial masses.
Radiation-induced cardiomyopathy is not supported and is a different mechanism.
Pericardial disease is a related involvement pattern, not secondary cardiac lymphoma itself.
